scenario: A personal access token with organization-wide write scope leaks through a laptop, log, or pasted configuration and is used to read or modify private repositories.
threat_source: External attacker using a stolen credential
affected_assets: Private repositories; Actions secrets; connected services
treatment: Restrict classic tokens, require approval and short lifetimes for fine-grained tokens, enable push protection, and review active tokens quarterly.

scenario: A compromised or retagged third-party action exfiltrates repository secrets or cloud credentials during a workflow run.
threat_source: Supply-chain attacker through a marketplace or public action
affected_assets: Actions secrets; cloud deployment credentials; build artifacts
treatment: Allow only listed actions pinned to full commit SHAs, keep the default token read-only, scope secrets to environments, and replace stored cloud keys with OIDC.

scenario: A former contractor remains an outside collaborator with write access after the engagement ends and retains or alters code.
threat_source: Former insider or takeover of a dormant account
treatment: Record a sponsor and end date for every outside collaborator, run a dated quarterly review, and test that removal ends access.

scenario: A private repository holding internal tooling, historical credentials, or client data is made public by mistake and is indexed within minutes.
affected_assets: Repository content; secrets in history; firm reputation
treatment: Limit visibility changes to owners, block public repository creation by members, keep secret scanning active, and alert on visibility change events.

scenario: An AI coding agent or automation with write access to production repositories merges or pushes unreviewed changes that alter deployment behavior.
threat_source: Agent error or prompt injection through issue and pull request content
affected_assets: Production repositories; deployment pipelines; downstream systems
treatment: Require reviewed pull requests on protected branches, prevent Actions from approving pull requests, gate production environments with human reviewers, and limit agent repositories.

scenario: A member account without phishing-resistant second factor is phished or session-hijacked and used to read private repositories and approve pull requests.
affected_assets: Member accounts; private repositories; review integrity
treatment: Require 2FA with secure methods, enforce SAML SSO and SCIM where the plan allows, and require a second reviewer for production changes.

scenario: The sole organization owner leaves or loses access and nobody can administer billing, membership, or security settings.
affected_assets: The organization; every repository and setting
treatment: Keep at least two accountable owners with deputies, document the ownership transfer runbook, and export membership on a schedule.

scenario: An API key or cloud credential is committed to a repository and later harvested by a scanner or a compromised collaborator.
threat_source: Accidental commit followed by an opportunistic attacker
affected_assets: Connected SaaS and cloud accounts; data those services hold
treatment: Enable push protection with a limited bypass list, replace long-lived cloud credentials with OIDC, and rotate any secret that reaches history.

scenario: A pull request from a fork triggers a workflow that runs untrusted code on a self-hosted runner with persistent credentials or internal network access.
threat_source: External contributor or attacker using a fork
affected_assets: Runner host; internal network; secrets on the runner
treatment: Require approval for fork workflows, keep self-hosted runners off public repositories, use ephemeral runners in restricted groups, and keep secrets out of runner hosts.

scenario: A known vulnerable dependency or code flaw ships in an internal automation because alerts are disabled or have no owner.
threat_source: External attacker exploiting a published vulnerability
treatment: Enable Dependabot alerts and security updates, run code scanning on production repositories, and assign every alert an owner and triage window.

scenario: An investigation cannot reconstruct who changed a setting or accessed a repository because audit events aged out of the native window or were never exported.
threat_source: Any incident combined with evidence loss
treatment: Schedule audit log exports or streaming before the 180-day window closes, test retrieval of a synthetic event, and store exports with the backup set.

scenario: An OAuth app or GitHub App installed by a member with broad permissions reads private repositories or acts on the organization without review.
affected_assets: Private repositories; organization data; webhook deliveries
treatment: Keep OAuth app access restrictions enabled, review installed GitHub Apps and their permissions quarterly, and suspend apps without an owner.
